name: The Passion of Saint John the Baptist
history: John the Baptist, the forerunner of Christ, told King Herod Antipas that it was not lawful for him to have his brother’s wife. Herod imprisoned him, and at a birthday feast, bound by a rash oath to the daughter of Herodias, had him beheaded. The Church honours his death as a martyrdom for truth and for Christ.
life: Saint Mark tells the story in full. Herod Antipas had married Herodias, the wife of his brother, and John rebuked him publicly. Herodias wanted John dead, but Herod feared him, knowing him to be a righteous and holy man, and liked to listen to him even when he was troubled by what he heard. At his birthday banquet her daughter danced for the guests, and Herod swore to give her whatever she asked. Prompted by her mother, she asked for the head of John the Baptist on a dish. Herod was grieved, but would not go back on his oath before his guests. John’s disciples came and laid his body in a tomb. The historian Josephus places his imprisonment in the fortress of Machaerus, east of the Dead Sea. The feast is linked to a church at Sebaste in Samaria, where tradition placed his tomb.
prayerTo: Saint John the Baptist, you prepared the way of the Lord and gave your life rather than keep silent about the truth. Pray that I may decrease so that Christ may increase in me. Give me courage to speak the truth with love, even when it is unwelcome, and to keep faith to the end. Amen.
penance: Abstain from meat or from a favourite food today in memory of the Forerunner, and keep a promise you have been putting off.
meditation: He must increase, but I must decrease. Where is your own pride getting in the way of Christ today?
